classification.difficultyReason: Compare four technology plots with a common vertex and explain geometrically how the sign of the leading coefficient controls the existence of x-intercepts.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Use computer graphing software to plot on the one number plane the parabola $y=a(x-1)^2-2$ for the following values of $a$.

answer.short: $y=2(x-1)^2-2$; solid curve on the shared graph.
answer.worked: Enter $y=2(x-1)^2-2$ in the graphing software. Its vertex is $(1,-2)$, it is concave up, and it passes through $(0,0)$ and $(2,0)$. Keep this curve on the same axes as the other three.

answer.short: $y=(x-1)^2-2$; dashed curve on the shared graph.
answer.worked: Enter $y=(x-1)^2-2$ on the same coordinate plane. Its vertex is $(1,-2)$, it is concave up, and it passes through $(0,-1)$ and $(2,-1)$.

answer.short: $y=-(x-1)^2-2$; dotted curve on the shared graph.
answer.worked: Enter $y=-(x-1)^2-2$ on the same coordinate plane. Its vertex is $(1,-2)$, it is concave down, and it passes through $(0,-3)$ and $(2,-3)$.

answer.short: $y=-2(x-1)^2-2$; dash-dot curve on the shared graph.
answer.worked: Enter $y=-2(x-1)^2-2$ on the same coordinate plane. Its vertex is $(1,-2)$, it is concave down, and it passes through $(0,-4)$ and $(2,-4)$.

spec.description: One shared coordinate plane containing all four requested parabolas. Solid, dashed, dotted and dash-dot strokes distinguish the four series; all meet at (1,-2).
spec.answerVisibility: Answer editions only; no supplied graph is printed in the student question.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Which point do all these parabolas pass through?

answer.worked: At $x=1$, $y=a(1-1)^2-2=-2$ for every listed value of $a$. All four parabolas therefore pass through $(1,-2)$.

children.label: c
children.prompt: For which values of $a$ does the parabola have $x$-intercepts?

answer.worked: The graphs with $a=1$ and $a=2$ cross the $x$-axis. More generally, the parabola has $x$-intercepts when $a>0$.

children.label: d
children.prompt: Explain your answer to part c geometrically.

answer.short: The vertex is below the $x$-axis, so the parabola intersects the $x$-axis only when it is concave up.
answer.worked: Every parabola has vertex $(1,-2)$, below the $x$-axis. When $a>0$, it is concave up and rises on both sides of the vertex, crossing the $x$-axis twice. When $a<0$, it is concave down and its maximum value is $-2$, so it cannot reach the $x$-axis.
